term.abilityScores: The six scores that define your hero, from 3 (feeble) to 20 (legendary). What matters most is the modifier in front: you add it to nearly every roll you make.
term.armorClass: Armor Class (AC) is how hard you are to hit. An attacker rolls a d20 and adds its bonuses; it hits only if the total meets or beats this number. Armor, shields, and Dexterity raise it.
term.attackRoll: Roll a d20 and add this bonus; you hit if the total meets or beats the target's Armor Class. The bonus is your ability modifier plus your Proficiency Bonus; damage adds only the ability modifier. On a Critical Hit you roll all the attack's damage dice twice (including extra dice like Sneak Attack) and total them; your modifier is still added only once.
term.initiative: Initiative sets the turn order. When combat starts, everyone rolls a d20 and adds this bonus; the highest acts first.
term.speed: Speed is how far you can move on your turn, alongside your action. Difficult terrain costs double.
term.proficiencyBonus: Your training bonus. Add it to every roll you are proficient in: trained skills, saving throws, weapon attacks, and your spells. It grows with level, from +2 at level 1 to +6 at level 20.
term.hitPoints: Hit Points (HP) are your stamina and will to keep fighting. Damage lowers them; rest and healing restore them. At 0 you fall unconscious and start making death saving throws.
term.hitDice: Your personal healing pool, one die per level. During a Short Rest you can spend Hit Dice: roll each die, add your Constitution modifier, and regain that many hit points.
term.passiveScore: What you notice without rolling: 10 plus the skill's bonus. The DM checks it quietly, for example to see whether you spot a hidden creature.
term.savingThrow: A d20 roll to resist a danger: dodging a fireball, shaking off a charm, enduring poison. The threat decides which ability you use; proficiency adds your Proficiency Bonus.
term.skillCheck: When the outcome is uncertain, the DM calls for a check: roll a d20 and add the skill's bonus. The dot marks skills you are proficient in.
term.spellSaveDc: How hard your spells are to resist. When a spell forces a saving throw, the target rolls a d20 plus its bonuses and must meet or beat this number.
term.spellAttack: The bonus you add to a d20 when a spell asks for an attack roll against a target's Armor Class, like a hurled flame.
term.spellSlot: The fuel for casting. Each spell of level 1 or higher spends one slot of that level or higher; cantrips are free. Slots return when you rest.
term.cantrip: A minor spell you can cast at will, without spending a spell slot. It never needs preparing; it is always ready.
term.preparedSpells: The spells you currently have ready to cast. After a Long Rest you can swap which spells you prepare, choosing from your class list.
term.concentration: Some spells last only while you concentrate. You can concentrate on one spell at a time, and taking damage forces a Constitution saving throw to keep it going.
term.ritual: A spell cast as a ritual takes 10 extra minutes but does not spend a spell slot.
term.components: What casting requires: V means speaking magic words, S a free hand for gestures, M a material such as a focus or a component pouch.
term.exhaustion: Exhaustion comes in levels of deep fatigue. Each level gives −2 to every d20 roll and slows you by 5 feet; at level 6 you die. A Long Rest removes one level.
term.pointBuy: A fair way to assign scores: every ability starts at 8 and you spend 27 points to raise them, up to 15 before bonuses. Higher scores cost more points.
term.feat: A special talent that gives your character an edge beyond class features. Origin feats come from your background; at later levels you can take one instead of an ability boost.
term.multiclass: Taking your next level in a different class instead of your current one. You keep everything you already have; the levels of all your classes add up to your total.
term.weaponSimple: An easy weapon to use without special training: clubs, daggers, spears. Almost every class is proficient with all Simple weapons.
term.weaponMartial: A weapon that demands real combat training: swords, axes, bows. Mostly the warrior classes are proficient with Martial weapons.
term.weaponFinesse: Attack with Strength or Dexterity, whichever suits you: the same ability counts for both the attack roll and the damage.
term.weaponLight: Small enough for two-weapon fighting: after you attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action with a different Light weapon, adding no ability modifier to its damage.
term.weaponHeavy: Built for strong hands: you have Disadvantage on attack rolls with it if your Strength is below 13 (melee) or your Dexterity is below 13 (ranged).
term.weaponReach: Adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, including for opportunity attacks.
term.weaponTwoHanded: Requires both hands when you attack with it; the rest of the time one hand is enough to carry it.
term.weaponVersatile: Wield it with one or two hands: with both hands, its damage uses the die shown in parentheses instead.
term.weaponThrown: You can throw it to make a ranged attack, using the same ability modifier as in melee. The two numbers are its normal and maximum throwing distance.
term.weaponAmmunition: Attacking requires ammunition: each shot expends one piece, and after the battle you can recover half of what you used. The two numbers are its normal and maximum range; beyond the first you attack with Disadvantage.
term.weaponLoading: Slow to reload: you can fire only one shot whenever you use an action, Bonus Action, or Reaction to attack with it, no matter how many attacks you could normally make.
term.masteryCleave: Weapon mastery: when you hit a creature in melee, you can swing through with one extra attack against a second creature within 5 feet of it (no ability modifier to that damage). Once per turn.
term.masteryGraze: Weapon mastery: even when your attack misses, the target still takes damage equal to the ability modifier you attacked with.
term.masteryNick: Weapon mastery: you can make the Light property's extra attack as part of the Attack action itself, instead of spending your Bonus Action. Once per turn.
term.masteryPush: Weapon mastery: when you hit, you can push the target up to 10 feet straight away from you, if it is Large or smaller.
term.masterySap: Weapon mastery: when you hit, the target has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.
term.masterySlow: Weapon mastery: when you hit and deal damage, the target's Speed drops by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.
term.masteryTopple: Weapon mastery: when you hit, you can force the target to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 + your attack modifier + Proficiency Bonus) or fall Prone.
term.masteryVex: Weapon mastery: when you hit and deal damage, you gain Advantage on your next attack roll against that target before the end of your next turn.
term.heroicInspiration: A boon the DM grants for heroic moments. While you hold it you can expend it to reroll any die you just rolled, and you must use the new roll. You can hold only one. Tap the token when you receive it; tap again when you spend it.
term.bardicInspirationDie: A die an ally Bard gives you (d6–d12); you can hold only one at a time. Within the next hour, when you fail a D20 Test, you can roll it and add the result, possibly turning the failure into a success; the die is expended when rolled. Tap the size you receive; tap again when you roll it.
term.encounterXp: Experience Points (XP) rate a monster's threat. This is the encounter's total, added up from each monster's XP, which the app weighs against your party's XP budget to grade how hard the fight is.
term.encounterDifficulty: How hard this fight is likely to be. Low is an easy win, Moderate a real fight, High is dangerous, and Over High is likely deadly. The grade comes from the monsters' total XP measured against your party's budget.
term.challengeRating: Challenge Rating (CR) is a monster's rough power level. Pick one and the app uses its standard XP to weigh this monster into the encounter's difficulty grade. Leave it blank for a quick improvised NPC that stays uncounted.
term.attunement: Some magic items only work once you bond with them, called attunement. Bonding takes a Short Rest; you can be attuned to three items at a time, and each attuned item fills one of those slots.
term.magicRarity: Rarity rates how powerful and hard to find a magic item is, from Common up through Uncommon, Rare, Very Rare, and Legendary, to the one-of-a-kind Artifact. Rarer items are stronger and, in most games, harder to come by.
term.blinded: While Blinded you can't see, so any check that needs sight fails. Your attack rolls have Disadvantage, and attack rolls against you have Advantage.
term.charmed: While Charmed you can't attack the one who charmed you or aim anything harmful at them, and they have Advantage on checks to sway you socially.
term.deafened: While Deafened you can't hear, so any check that needs hearing fails.
term.frightened: While Frightened you have Disadvantage on checks and attack rolls as long as you can see what scares you, and you can't choose to move closer to it.
term.grappled: While Grappled your Speed is 0, and you have Disadvantage on attack rolls against anyone except the one holding you. They can drag you along as they move.
term.incapacitated: While Incapacitated you can't take actions, Bonus Actions, or Reactions, you can't speak, and your Concentration breaks.
term.invisible: While Invisible others can't see you: your attack rolls have Advantage and attack rolls against you have Disadvantage, unless something can see you anyway. You also roll Initiative with Advantage.
term.paralyzed: While Paralyzed you are Incapacitated and can't move or speak. You fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws, attack rolls against you have Advantage, and any hit from within 5 feet is a Critical Hit.
term.petrified: While Petrified you are turned to stone: Incapacitated, unable to move or speak, and unaware of your surroundings. Attack rolls against you have Advantage, you fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws, and you have Resistance to all damage.
term.poisoned: While Poisoned you have Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.
term.prone: While Prone you're on the ground and can only crawl. Your attack rolls have Disadvantage; attackers within 5 feet have Advantage against you, those farther away Disadvantage. Standing up costs half your Speed.
term.restrained: While Restrained your Speed is 0. Your attack rolls and Dexterity saving throws have Disadvantage, and attack rolls against you have Advantage.
term.stunned: While Stunned you are Incapacitated: no actions, Bonus Actions, or Reactions. You fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws, and attack rolls against you have Advantage.
term.unconscious: While Unconscious you are Incapacitated and Prone, you drop what you're holding, and you can't move, speak, or notice anything. You fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws, attack rolls against you have Advantage, and any hit from within 5 feet is a Critical Hit.
term.base-dash: Dash gives you extra movement this turn equal to your Speed, so you can usually move twice as far.
term.base-dodge: Dodge: until the start of your next turn, attack rolls against you have Disadvantage and you have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws. You lose this if you become Incapacitated or your Speed drops to 0.
term.base-disengage: Disengage: for the rest of this turn, moving away from enemies doesn't provoke any Opportunity Attack.
term.base-help: Help gives an ally Advantage: on their next ability check with a skill or tool you're proficient in, or on their next attack roll against an enemy within 5 feet of you. It lasts until the start of your next turn.
term.base-hide: Hide when enemies can't see you, behind solid cover or in thick darkness or fog: make a DC 15 Dexterity (Stealth) check. On a success you have the Invisible condition while you stay hidden.
term.base-influence: Influence: try to change a creature's attitude by persuading, deceiving, intimidating, performing, or calming an animal. The DM picks the check and how hard it is; a creature already willing may simply agree.
term.base-magic: Magic: cast a spell that takes an action, or use a magic item or special ability that needs the Magic action.
term.base-ready: Ready lets you act later, on someone else's turn: choose something you can notice as the trigger and what you'll do, then use your Reaction when it happens.
term.base-search: Search: look or sense for something hidden or unclear with a Wisdom check, such as Perception to spot a hidden creature or Insight to read someone's mood.
term.base-study: Study: recall or work out what you know with an Intelligence check, such as Arcana about magic, History about the past, or Investigation to piece clues together.
term.base-utilize: Utilize: use a nonmagical object that takes an action, like pulling a lever or lighting a lamp.
term.base-object-interaction: Interact with an Object: once per turn you can handle one object for free while you move or act, like drawing a sword or opening a door. A second one in the same turn takes the Utilize action.
term.base-grapple: Grapple is an Unarmed Strike: with a free hand, grab a creature within 5 feet that is at most one size larger than you. It makes a Strength or Dexterity saving throw; if it fails, it has the Grappled condition.
term.base-shove: Shove is an Unarmed Strike against a creature within 5 feet that is at most one size larger than you. It makes a Strength or Dexterity saving throw; if it fails, you push it 5 feet away or give it the Prone condition.
term.base-escape-grapple: Escape: while Grappled, use your action for a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check against the escape DC. On a success you're free.
term.base-opportunity-attack: Opportunity Attack: when an enemy you can see moves out of your reach, you can use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it. A creature that takes the Disengage action avoids it.
